frontier_hypothesis.falsification_test: Compare settings where experience differs while other inputs are matched. The hypothesis fails if integrated information does not stay bounded with experience, or if fixing cause removes no part of the effect.
frontier_hypothesis.assumptions: Assumes each cited relation holds in the same setting and that effects carry across the shared term.

co_mentions.quote: Moreover, the way an experience feels is accounted for by how that cause–effect power is structured.

Physicalism assumes an operational criterion for assessing the existence of things outside of my own experience: I can be confident that something exists—whether it is my hand, a rock, a distant star, or an elementary particle—if I can show or infer that it has cause–effect power, in the sense that it can “take and make a difference,” and it does so in a way that is reliable and persisting.

If every experience is characterized by the five essential properties of phenomenal existence, the substrate of consciousness should be characterized by the same properties in terms of physical existence, understood operationally as cause–effect power established by observing and manipulating its constituting units.

co_mentions.quote: Integrated Information (Phi) quantifies how much the integrated cause/effect structure of the global neural network fails to be accounted for by any partitioned version of it.

The integrated cause or effect information of the system S over the partition θ, is defined as the intrinsic cause or effect information of S, with informativeness defined relative to the partitioned repertoire instead of the unconstrained repertoire.
Accordingly, since a system must both take and make a difference to exist, the system integrated information for a given partition θ is defined as the minimum of its integrated cause

predictions.quote: If every experience is characterized by the five essential properties of phenomenal existence, the substrate of consciousness should be characterized by the same properties in terms of physical existence, understood operationally as cause–effect power established by observing and manipulating its constituting units.

Instead, the identity should be understood in an explanatory sense: the intrinsic (subjective) feeling of the experience can be explained extrinsically (objectively, i.e., operationally or physically) in terms of cause–effect power [27].

setups.quote: Recent experiments (gedanken or otherwise) and theorems in quantum mechanics (QM), such as new iterations on Wigner's friend and delayed choice, have led many people to claim that QM is not compatible with determinate and intersubjectively consistent experience (what some call absoluteness of observed events), such as experiences of experimental outcomes.

In the following section, we introduce the necessary terms to define how to falsify this class of theories: how measurement of a physical system’s observables results in datasets (Section 2.1), how a theory makes use of those datasets to offer predictions about consciousness (Section 2.2), how an experimenter makes inferences about a physical system’s experiences (Section 2.3), and finally how falsification of a theory occurs when there is a mismatch between a theory’s prediction and an experimenter’s inference (Section 2.4).
That is, experiences themselves are never identified or used in obs, but are rather inferred based on some dataset o that contains report or other behavioural indicators.
Next we explore how the datasets in O are used to make predictions about the experience of a physical
A theory of consciousness makes predictions about the experience of some physical system in some configuration, state, or dynamics, p, based on some dataset o.

Formally, this means that a prediction considers an experimental dataset o ∈ O (determined by obs) and specifies an element of the experience space E. We denote this as pred, for “prediction,” which is a map from O to E. The details of how individual datasets are being used to make predictions again do not matter for the sake of our investigation.
